# / between INTERVAL and INT64 values
# https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/operators#interval_arithmetic_operators
#
# Whether BigQuery truncates a quotient finer than a microsecond toward zero, as GoogleSQL does
# without nanosecond precision, and how it reports a division by zero.

SELECT INTERVAL 1 MICROSECOND / 2
?> "0-0 0 0:0:0"

SELECT INTERVAL -1 MICROSECOND / 2
?> "0-0 0 0:0:0"

SELECT INTERVAL 1 SECOND / 3
?> "0-0 0 0:0:0.333333"

SELECT INTERVAL -1 SECOND / 3
?> "0-0 0 -0:0:0.333333"

SELECT INTERVAL 1 YEAR / 0
?> error: Interval division by zero

SELECT 6 / INTERVAL 2 DAY
?> error: No matching signature for operator /
  Argument types: INT64, INTERVAL
  Signature: FLOAT64 / FLOAT64
    Argument 2: Unable to coerce type INTERVAL to expected type FLOAT64
  Signature: NUMERIC / NUMERIC
    Argument 2: Unable to coerce type INTERVAL to expected type NUMERIC
  Signature: BIGNUMERIC / BIGNUMERIC
    Argument 2: Unable to coerce type INTERVAL to expected type BIGNUMERIC
  Signature: INTERVAL / INT64
    Argument 1: Unable to coerce type INT64 to expected type INTERVAL at [1:8]
